tiersPage.title: The four kinds of room
tiersPage.intro: Every topic is one of four kinds, and the kind decides who gets in, who can read what, and whether we can read your chat. This page says exactly what each one does. Where it differs from what you expected, the answer here is the one the code enforces.

table.caption: What each kind of room does

public.name: Public
public.summary: Open to everyone, and the one kind whose chat history we can read.

private.name: Private
private.summary: Anyone can see it exists and read its posts; getting into the conversation needs an invite link.

secret.name: Secret
secret.summary: Invisible unless someone sends you the link.

find.hidden: Nobody — it is hidden from every list

posts.signedIn: Anyone signed in, member or not

tiersPage.chatAccess: Members only, in every kind of room

history.window: Only what the person who invited them chose to share — a recent slice, not the whole history

operator.yesDetail: We hold a key to this room's history so that anyone who joins later can read it. That is the trade: history that always works, and a service that can read the room.
operator.noDetail: We move the messages without being able to open them. Nobody at OpenStoa can read this room.

sections.historyTitle: What you see when you join a room that has been talking for a while
sections.historyBody: In a public room you see everything, because we hold the key and hand it over the moment you arrive. In a private or secret room we cannot do that, so history only reaches you if the person inviting you chooses to include a recent slice with the invite — and it is a slice, not the whole conversation. In a direct message the question never comes up: nobody joins later. Whatever history does reach you arrives with its pictures: an image is sealed with the same key as the message it came in, so there is nothing extra to share and nothing that can be shared by mistake.
sections.retentionBody: Whoever creates a topic chooses how long its chat history is kept: forever, a year, 90 days, or 30 days. Once a message falls outside that window it is deleted for everyone, so a member who joins later sees less.
sections.retentionCeiling: Treat the window as a ceiling, not a deletion deadline. Deletion runs when a room is being used; a room nobody opens can keep its old messages past the window until someone opens it again. If you need a guaranteed deletion date, this is not it yet.
sections.devicesTitle: Your history lives on your devices
sections.devicesBody: Your chat history is encrypted with keys held by the devices you use — a browser profile and the app are two different devices, even on the same machine. Adding a new one is fine: it restores your history from your own backup.
sections.devicesWarning: But if you lose every device you have used and you did not save a recovery code, that history is gone. Not withheld — gone. Nobody, including us, can bring it back, because nobody else ever had the key. Save your recovery code.
sections.mediaBody: Images you send now are encrypted the same way messages are. Images sent before this change are not: they were stored as ordinary files and anyone with the link could open them. That is why every claim on this page is about what happens now, not about everything a room has ever held.
sections.postsVsChatTitle: Private topics: posts are open, the conversation is not
sections.postsVsChatBody: A private topic is listed and anyone signed in can read its posts — what is private is the chat. You get into that with an invite link, and the same link is what carries the keys for the slice of history the inviter chose to share. A secret topic goes further: it is hidden from every list, and its posts are members-only too.
